newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Plessey, Lucent sign memorandum.
newsitem.headline: Plessey, Lucent sign memorandum.

text.p: South African electronics firm Plessey Corp Ltd said on Wednesday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with U.S-based Lucent Technologies Inc on participation in a two billion rand contract awarded by utility Telkom.
Lucent, together with Franco-South African Alcatel Altech Telecoms (AAT), on Tuesday won a two billion rand radio systems contract from Telkom.
Plessey's involvement in the Telkom deal will cover the provision of network planning, project management and installation which will be done through its projects division.
Lucent said in a statement discussions over Plessey's scope and involvement in the Telkom deal were still under way, but added that Plessey would play a "major role".
These plans were in line with a commitment to supporting local industry through strategic partnerships and to sub-contracting a part of the work to empowerment groups.
Plessey is jointly controlled by black firm Worldwide Africa Investments Holdings and investment company Sankorp.
The statement said that Plessey had considerable experience in involving small businesses and sub-contractors.
Telkom said earlier that the bulk of its contract had been awarded to AAT.

The contract, which aims to connect 420,000 telephone lines in previously under-serviced areas, covers the supply, planning and installation of standalone Digital Enhanced Cordless Telecommunications (DECT) systems and Time Division Multiple Access (TDMA) with DECT tail systems.
Telkom said that 90 percent of the TDMA contact had been awarded to AAT, with the remaining 10 percent going to Lucent.
On the DECT contract, the exact proportions had not been worked out yet but Telkom said that AAT would secure between 50 and 60 percent and Lucent between 40 and 50 percent.
